# Email Marketing for Pet Groomers  
_Keep Clients Coming Back, Automatically_

⏱ 60 minutes to set up 💰 Free to start 📧 No tech skills needed

F

M

[Fredrik Filipsson](https://mainstreetaiautomation.com/about/fredrik-filipsson) & [Morten Andersen](https://mainstreetaiautomation.com/about/morten-andersen)Co-founders, Main Street AI · built multi-million dollar businesses with AI

Your happiest clients forget to rebook, not because they don't love your work, but because life gets busy. Email marketing fixes that. This tutorial shows you how to set up a complete email system that automatically welcomes new clients, reminds them before appointments, and gently nudges them to rebook, all while you're busy with furry customers.

$42ROI per $1 spent on email

65%Repeat clients from referrals

FreeMailchimp up to 500 contacts

8 hrsSaved per month after setup

**Affiliate Disclosure:** Some links on this page are affiliate links. If you sign up through them, Main Street AI earns a small commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend tools we'd genuinely suggest to a friend. [Learn more](https://mainstreetaiautomation.com/privacy).

The Problem

## Why Most Grooming Clients Only Come Back _Sometimes_

You do a great job. The dog leaves looking fabulous. The owner is thrilled. And then… six months go by before they book again. Not because they were unhappy, because nobody reminded them.

Email marketing is essentially a polite, automated reminder system. Once you set it up, it runs in the background sending the right message at the right time, whether that's a welcome note for a new client, a rebooking nudge at the 6-week mark, or a "your dog might be overdue for a bath" check-in.

### Without Email Marketing

*   Clients rebook only when they remember
*   New clients get no follow-up after first visit
*   You manually call or text to fill empty slots
*   No way to announce slow-day specials
*   Client list sits unused in your booking app

#### With Email Marketing

*   Automated rebooking reminders go out on schedule
*   Welcome sequences build loyalty from day one
*   Slow day? One email fills your calendar
*   Seasonal promotions reach every client instantly
*   Your list becomes your most valuable business asset

Tools Used in This Tutorial

[Mailchimp, Free](https://login.mailchimp.com/signup/)

[ActiveCampaign, $15/mo](https://www.activecampaign.com/free-trial/)

[Calendly, Free](https://calendly.com/signup)

Your booking app

01

### Create Your Free Mailchimp Account and Audience

Mailchimp (think of it as your email command center) is free for up to 500 contacts, more than enough to get started. "Audience" is just Mailchimp's word for your email list.

**Go to [mailchimp.com](https://login.mailchimp.com/signup/)** and click "Sign Up Free." Use your business email (not a personal Gmail).

During setup, Mailchimp asks a few questions. Answer honestly, it helps them configure your account correctly:

*   **Business name:** Your grooming salon name exactly as clients know it
*   **Industry:** Pick "Other" → type "Pet Services"
*   **Audience name:** "\[Your Salon Name\] Clients" works perfectly

📸

Screenshot: Mailchimp audience creation screen with fields highlighted

💡 Pro Tip

Mailchimp will ask for a physical mailing address, this is legally required for email marketing (CAN-SPAM law). You can use a P.O. box or your salon's address. It shows at the bottom of every email you send.

02

### Import Your Existing Client List

You probably have client contact info in your booking app, a spreadsheet, or your phone. Let's get it into Mailchimp.

**Option A, Import from CSV (most common):**

1.  Export your client list from your booking software (look for "Export Clients" or "Download CSV")
2.  In Mailchimp, go to **Audience → Add Contacts → Import Contacts**
3.  Upload your CSV file and match the columns (First Name, Last Name, Email)
4.  Tag these contacts as "Existing Clients", you'll use this later

**Option B, Connect Calendly directly:** If you use Calendly for bookings, go to **Integrations → Mailchimp** and connect the two. Every new booking automatically adds the client to your Mailchimp audience. This is the easiest setup.

📸

Screenshot: Mailchimp "Import Contacts" screen with CSV upload option

📋 Important

Only import clients who've given you their email for business purposes. Grooming customers who booked with you have implicitly consented to receive business communications. You don't need a separate opt-in for existing clients, but always include an unsubscribe link (Mailchimp adds this automatically).

03

### Build Your 3-Email Welcome Sequence

A welcome sequence is a series of emails that goes out automatically when someone new joins your list. Think of it as a warm handshake that happens even when you're elbow-deep in a golden retriever's bath.

In Mailchimp, go to **Automations → Customer Journeys → Start Building**. Choose "Welcome new contacts" as your starting point.

### Email 1, Sent immediately after signup

Subject: Welcome to \[Salon Name\], Here's what to expect 🐾

Hi \[First Name\], We're so happy \[Pet Name\] found us! (And we're pretty sure \[Pet Name\] is excited too, though they might not admit it yet.) Here's what you can expect from us: • Every appointment includes \[list your signature services\] • We'll send a reminder 24 hours before each visit • After each appointment, we'll ask how we did Questions? Reply to this email, it goes straight to \[your name\]. Your next appointment is on \[date\]. We can't wait to see \[Pet Name\]! \[Your name\] \[Salon name\] | \[Phone\]

### Email 2, Sent 3 days after first appointment

Subject: How did \[Pet Name\]'s first visit go?

Hi \[First Name\], We hope \[Pet Name\] is still enjoying that fresh-groomed feeling! A quick question: was there anything about your first visit we could improve? We read every reply personally. Also, here's a grooming tip we share with all new clients: \[Insert one helpful tip: e.g., "Brushing your dog 2–3x per week between appointments keeps mats from forming and makes each grooming session faster (and cheaper for you!)"\] Ready to book \[Pet Name\]'s next appointment? We recommend every \[6–8\] weeks for \[breed\] to keep their coat in great shape. \[Book Now → link to your booking page\] See you soon! \[Your name\]

### Email 3, Sent 5 weeks after first appointment

Subject: Is \[Pet Name\] due for a groom? 🐶

Hi \[First Name\], It's been about 5 weeks since \[Pet Name\]'s last visit, which means their coat is probably sta

# Email Marketing for Dog Groomers: Start With Permission

Posted on [11/03/202603/11/2026](https://www.woofspark.com.au/email-marketing-for-dog-groomers/) by [Marine Ponchaut](https://www.woofspark.com.au/author/marine-ponchaut/)

[](https://www.woofspark.com.au/email-marketing-for-dog-groomers/)

11  
Mar

Your booking system is full of email addresses. Hundreds, maybe. It’s tempting to export the lot, write a cheerful “we miss you!” email and hit send.

Hold that thought for ten minutes. In Australia, a marketing email needs the person’s consent first, and booking a groom isn’t the same as saying yes to marketing. The good news is that a list of clients who’ve actually asked to hear from you is the list you want anyway: people who are glad to see your name in their inbox. Building one properly isn’t hard.

The short version

Ask clients to opt in, and keep a record of when and how they said yes. Send something genuinely useful about their dog. Say who you are in every email, and make unsubscribing easy. The [ACMA](https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam) explains the rules in plain English.

[Get the free 90-day plan →](https://www.woofspark.com.au/free-90-day-dog-grooming-business-plan/?utm_content=email-marketing-for-dog-groomers-quick)

## 1\. Get permission the right way

Under Australia’s [Spam Act](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A01214/latest/text), you need consent before you send marketing messages. Every message must say who it’s from and how to contact you, and every one needs a working unsubscribe.

The clearest kind of consent is **express consent**: the person knowingly agrees to get marketing emails from you. They might tick a box on your booking form, fill in a sign-up form, or say yes in person or on the phone. Keep a record of who said yes, when and how. If it’s ever questioned, it’s up to you to show the consent.

What about clients who’ve booked before? **Inferred consent** can apply in some ongoing relationships, where someone gave you their address and would reasonably expect marketing from you. But the ACMA says it’s less reliable than express consent, and it doesn’t cover someone who has simply bought from you once. When in doubt, ask.

One thing you can’t do: send an email asking for consent. That request is a marketing message itself.

**Opt-in wording you can adapt**

☐ Yes, I’d like occasional grooming tips, seasonal booking reminders and salon news by email from \[your salon name\]. I can unsubscribe at any time.

Leave the box unticked, and keep it separate from your booking terms, so it’s a real choice.

Before you hit send

Can I email this client?

*   They ticked the box, or said yes and you noted the date**Yes**That’s express consent. Keep the record of who said yes, when and how.
*   They’ve booked a groom but never agreed to emails**Not yet**A past booking isn’t permission by itself. Ask on your form or at pick-up; you can’t email to ask.
*   They unsubscribed, even years ago**No**Act on it within five working days and keep them off your list, even when you change tools.

## 2\. Build your list where it makes sense

*   **On your new-client form:** a separate, unticked box like the one above.
*   **At pick-up:** “Would you like our coat-care tips by email?” If they say yes, note it on their record with the date.
*   **On your website:** a simple sign-up form that says what you’ll send and how often.
*   **In the salon:** a sign or QR code that leads to the same sign-up form.

Before you import an old client spreadsheet into an email tool, check every address. Leave out anyone without clear consent, and anyone who has ever unsubscribed. Keep unsubscribes blocked when you change tools, too. The ACMA lists adding people automatically after a one-off purchase or an enquiry as one of the [common mistakes](https://www.acma.gov.au/telemarketing-and-e-marketing-common-issues-and-mistakes) businesses make.

## 3\. Send something they’ll be glad to open

The emails clients open are the ones about their dog. A few first topics that work for a grooming business:

*   Getting ready for summer: keeping a curly coat comfortable in the heat
*   Christmas grooms: when the diary usually fills, and how to secure a spot
*   Brushing between grooms: a simple routine that keeps tangles away
*   Something new: puppy introduc

Then he ran the same search through Scrap.io. 59,322 US pet groomers. With emails, phones, websites, social profiles: the whole thing. In about two minutes.

Forty-one versus fifty-nine thousand. Brutal.

## The Pet Grooming Market in 2026: Why These Leads Are Gold

### Market size & growth

The US pet grooming industry hit **$14.5 billion in 2026** ([SchedulingKit](https://schedulingkit.com/statistics/pet-grooming-industry-statistics)). That's not a typo. Fourteen point five billion dollars spent on washing, clipping, and pampering animals. And the growth isn't slowing down. [IBISWorld counts roughly 193,000 businesses](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/industry/pet-grooming-boarding/1735/) in the grooming and boarding space across the US.

Pet owners are spending an average of **$510 per year on grooming**, with 42% increasing that spend year over year ([SchedulingKit](https://schedulingkit.com/statistics/pet-grooming-industry-statistics)). That's a niche where people don't cut corners. Even during recessions, Fido still gets his bath.

### Types of groomers (salons, mobile, franchise)

Not all groomers are the same. You've got brick-and-mortar salons, mobile groomers driving around in those custom vans, franchise operations like PetSmart and Petco, and independent home-based pros clipping poodles in their garage. Mobile grooming alone is seeing **12-15% annual growth** ([SchedulingKit](https://schedulingkit.com/statistics/pet-grooming-industry-statistics)). That's massive.

And each type has wildly different needs. A mobile groomer wants portable equipment. A salon owner cares about booking software. A franchise manager needs bulk supply deals. One-size-fits-all marketing? Dead on arrival.

### Why B2B targets this niche

Here's why the **pet groomer email list** is such a hot commodity: these are small business owners with real budgets, recurring needs, and almost zero LinkedIn presence. You're not going to find **pet groomer contacts** on Sales Navigator. But they're all on Google Maps. Every single one of them. If you're in the business of selling grooming supplies, SaaS, insurance, or marketing services, these **pet grooming leads** are basically an untapped goldmine that most B2B teams completely ignore.

Similar dynamics apply to [veterinary email lists](https://scrap.io/veterinary-email-lists-complete-prospecting-guide), another pet industry vertical where the leads are sitting right there on Maps, waiting to be found.

## What's Actually Inside a Pet Groomer Email List?

### Standard fields (email, phone, address)

A **pet grooming email list** at its most basic gives you: business name, email address, phone number, physical address, and maybe a website. That's the minimum. Most legacy providers stop here and call it a day. (Spoiler: that's not enough.)

The real question isn't whether a list has emails. It's whether those emails _still work_. If you're wondering **how to get pet groomer emails** that don't bounce, the answer starts with data freshness. Grooming businesses open and close faster than you'd think. An email address from six months ago? Might as well be from 2019.

### Advanced data (social, tech, ad pixels, email classification)

Modern [email databases](https://scrap.io/articles/email-database) go way deeper. We're talking social media profiles (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok), tech stack detection on their websites, whether they run ad pixels, and, this is the big one, **email classification**. Is that email a generic info@ address, a personal inbox, a sales line? That distinction changes your entire outreach strategy.

With Scrap.io, each email gets classified automatically: individual (with first and last name extracted), contact, sales, marketing, or admin. You know exactly who you're writing to before you hit send.

_Video: Get Emails from Google Maps for Free (Scrap.io Tutorial)_

### Dog groomer vs pet groomer vs pet service

A **dog groomer email list** is a subset of the broader pet groomer category. Some databases lump everything together: dog groomers, cat groomers, mobile pet services, even pet sitters. If you're figuring out **how to find pet groomer contacts** for a specific sub-niche, you need a **pet groomer database** that lets you filter by category. Otherwise you're emailing cat groomers about dog shampoo. Awkward. And no, the **best pet groomer email list** isn't the biggest one. It's the one that lets you target precisely who you need.

![Scrap.io search interface to build a pet groomer email list from Google Maps](https://d21qib8yfs3w9j.cloudfront.net/1140/conversions/en-scp-search-resized-resized.jpg)

## Static Lists vs Live Data: The $2,000 Mistake

### How traditional list brokers work

Jake bought a "premium" **professional pet groomer email list** of 5,000 contacts for $800. His first campaign? 34% bounce rate. That's not marketing. That's setting money on fire.

Traditional list brokers compile data once, maybe twice a year. They scrape directories, buy old databases, stitch things together, slap a "verified" label on it, and sell it to you at a premium. By the time you get the file, a chunk of those businesses have moved, closed, or changed their email provider. Bottom line: you're paying top dollar for yesterday's leftovers. If
